About this page

A list of robotics and automation companies, including a supplier map. Five tabs: Companies (the company directory), Supplier map (who supplies the parts, in India and abroad), Analytics (charts for both), Supply chain (a visual flow and detailed information for each layer of a robot’s supply chain) and this README.

Company directory

What this is

A directory of robotics and automation companies, taken from the Google Sheet “Robotics & Automation Directory – MASTER”, 20 November 2026. It has two lists: India (companies based in India or with an India presence) and World (companies elsewhere). The two lists do not overlap and are never mixed.

Order of the list

Robotics companies come first. Below them, in this order and with serial numbers running straight on: Suppliers (Tier 2-3), then Aerospace & Space, Drones & UAVs and AV & Adjacent at the very end. Each segment has its own divider row in the list, and you can filter by segment. Suppliers, aerospace, drones and AV & adjacent companies sit in the India list when their country is India, and in the World list otherwise.

Search

Search looks through both the India and World lists at once, whichever list you are on. Matches show a List column so you can see where each company sits. Location and India-presence filters are paused while you search; segment, sub-category and headcount filters still apply. Clear the search box to go back to the list you were on.

Columns

  • Company, Website, LinkedIn: as listed in the sheet. Click a row to see the links.
  • Segment: Robotics, Suppliers (Tier 2-3), Aerospace & Space, Drones & UAVs or AV & Adjacent. Each segment keeps the same colour everywhere on this page.
  • Sub-category: the sheet’s own grouping inside a segment. For Suppliers this is the tier (Tier 2 or Tier 3).
  • HQ city: headquarters city. Some companies in the India list have headquarters abroad.
  • India presence (India list only): the sheet’s free-text note. The filter groups it into “HQ in India” and “Office or R&D in India” (everything that is not exactly “HQ”).
  • Country (World list only): country of headquarters.
  • Headcount: the size band as listed in the sheet. “Not listed” means the sheet has no value.
  • What they do: a one-line description, shown when you open a row.

Where the data comes from

This page shows a saved copy of the sheet, taken on 20 November 2026. Changes made to the sheet afterwards do not appear here until a new copy is attached.

Gaps in the data

—

Supplier map

A separate map of the suppliers behind robotics, built from the “India Robotics Supply Chain Map” sheet. Use the India and World buttons at the top, the same ones as the company lists, to switch between Indian suppliers (655 listings, 569 companies, in 20 categories such as motors, reducers, sensors, batteries and robot makers) and foreign suppliers (295 listings, 238 companies, with how each reaches India). It is separate from the company directory and from its Suppliers (Tier 2-3) segment.

  • Search and Filter: the search box looks through the supplier list you are viewing. Filters opens dropdowns: Category, State, Robot type and Made in for Indian suppliers; Category, Country and How it reaches India for foreign ones. Clear removes all filters and the search.
  • Made in: whether a product is made in India, assembled in India, designed in India but made abroad, or imported.
  • Size: “Unknown” means the company’s size could not be found publicly. Confidence (High, Medium, Low) reflects how strong the source is.
  • Robot type: “No direct robotics customer” means none was found, for example a raw-material supplier.
  • Company names link to the company’s website where the sheet’s source was the company’s own site.
  • A company that supplies several categories appears once per category; open a row to see the others.
  • The supplier charts are on the Analytics tab, below the company charts. They cover all suppliers and are not changed by the list filters.

Supply chain

The Supply chain tab has two views. Visual flow shows the 14 layers of a robot’s supply chain in order, in four stages, from raw materials to testing. Detailed information lists the 115 components with what each does, how hard it is to make, where it is mainly made and the supply risk. The layers are the Stage 1 taxonomy, a broader cut than the supplier categories.
